framework.name: Domain-Driven Design for Acting Systems
framework.author: Dzmitryi Kharlanau
framework.purpose: Extend practical Domain-Driven Design with explicit decision, autonomy, evidence and agent boundaries for systems where people, deterministic software and AI agents can all act.

position.thesis: Domain boundaries are no longer enough. Systems with AI agents also need explicit decision boundaries.
position.interpretation: A bounded context protects meaning. A decision boundary defines who may decide, what evidence may be used, how an action may be executed and how the outcome is checked.
position.non_claim: This is a personal working synthesis. It is not an official extension of Domain-Driven Design and it does not replace the original DDD strategic or tactical patterns.

what_remains_from_ddd.reason: People, code and agents need the same domain terms inside one context.
A model is valid only inside an explicit semantic boundary.
Cross-context relationships and translation still need to be designed rather than assumed.
Business consistency rules remain deterministic constraints even when an AI system assists the process.
Business facts remain useful for integration, observation and reconstruction of what happened.
Foreign semantics should be translated before they influence the local model.

extensions.name: Decision Boundary
extensions.description: Defines the authority, allowed evidence, deterministic rules, permitted judgment and action limits for one business decision.

extensions.name: Agent Contract
extensions.description: Defines the role of an agent inside a domain context, including readable data, callable tools, forbidden actions, approval rules and required evidence.

extensions.name: Evidence Model
extensions.description: Separates authoritative business truth from retrieved context, model output and observed execution evidence.

extensions.name: Autonomy Level
extensions.description: Makes the permitted degree of machine action explicit instead of hiding it inside prompts or application code.

extensions.name: Semantic Memory Boundary
extensions.description: Treats vector stores, knowledge graphs and retrieved documents as contextual memory, not transactional truth.

extensions.name: Evaluation Contract
extensions.description: Defines how a probabilistic component is tested against domain cases, failure modes and acceptable behavior before autonomy is increased.

design_units.name: Context
design_units.definition: The semantic boundary in which a domain model and language are valid.
design_units.design_question: Inside which boundary can this business meaning stay coherent?

design_units.name: Capability
design_units.definition: A business ability with an accountable owner and a stable purpose.
design_units.design_question: Who owns this ability and its outcome?

design_units.name: Contract
design_units.definition: The explicit interface through which contexts, systems or agents exchange intent and facts.
design_units.design_question: What may cross the boundary without leaking internal semantics?

design_units.name: Decision
design_units.definition: A domain choice with inputs, rules, judgment, authority, outcome and risk.
design_units.design_question: What must be decided, and which part may be probabilistic?

design_units.name: Event
design_units.definition: A durable statement that something relevant happened in the domain.
design_units.design_question: Which fact should remain observable after the action is complete?

design_units.name: Evidence
design_units.definition: The traceable information used to justify, review or reconstruct a decision and action.
design_units.design_question: What proves why this result was accepted?

classification.use: Rules that must always hold and should not be delegated to a probabilistic model.
A choice where several valid options exist and an AI model may rank, explain or propose within fixed constraints.
Interpretation or recommendation where a human or deterministic process keeps final authority.
A decision that requires facts or commitments owned by more than one bounded context and therefore needs explicit orchestration or negotiation.

agent_model.principle: An AI agent is a domain actor, not a new bounded context by default.
agent_model.placement_rule: Place the agent inside the business context whose language, decisions and contracts it uses. Create a separate bounded context only when it owns a genuinely separate domain model and lifecycle.
agent_model.tool_rule: Expose domain-shaped tools with narrow intent. Avoid generic database, shell or system-wide mutation capabilities as business interfaces.
agent_model.truth_rule: Agents may read, interpret and propose. They do not become the source of record by producing an answer.
agent_model.cross_context_rule: When an agent crosses a bounded context, require an explicit contract and translation just as for any other integration.

autonomy_levels.name: Recommend
autonomy_levels.agent_may: Evaluate options and recommend a next move.

autonomy_levels.name: Prepare
autonomy_levels.agent_may: Prepare a transaction, message, change set or workflow input without committing it.
autonomy_levels.typical_use: Draft order change, create support response, prepare master-data correction.

autonomy_levels.name: Execute with approval
autonomy_levels.agent_may: Execute a pre-defined action only after an explicit approval checkpoint.
autonomy_levels.human_role: Approves material action and handles exceptions.
autonomy_levels.typical_use: Controlled workflow action with traceable approval.

autonomy_levels.name: Bounded execution
autonomy_levels.agent_may: Execute without per-action approval inside narrow policy, value, time and scope limits.
autonomy_levels.human_role: Defines policy, observes outcomes and handles escalation.
autonomy_levels.typical_use: Low-risk reversible actions with strong deterministic guardrails.

memory_and_truth.name: Event Memory
memory_and_truth.may_authorize_action: only when event semantics and freshness are sufficient for the decision

memory_and_truth.name: Evidence Store
memory_and_truth.role: Why a decision or action happened

method.name: Explore
method.question: What business problem, language, events and decisions exist?

method.name: Bound
method.question: Where does meaning change and who owns the capability?

method.name: Contract
method.question: What is allowed to cross each boundary?

method.name: Decide
method.question: Which decisions are deterministic, advisory or judgment-based?

method.name: Act
method.question: Which actors may execute which domain operations?

method.name: Observe
method.question: What evidence shows what the system decided and did?

method.name: Learn
method.question: Which failures should change policy, evaluation or the model?

artifacts.purpose: Capture language, scope, owners, source-of-record objects, inbound and outbound relationships.
Map business abilities to ownership and system responsibility.
Define terms that humans, code, prompts, tools and events must use consistently.
List important business decisions, their authority, inputs, invariants, risk and permitted judgment.
Define one narrow executable domain operation with inputs, preconditions, permissions, effects and failure states.
Define a stable business fact, owner, schema, versioning and consumer expectations.
Define agent role, context, tools, data, autonomy, forbidden actions, escalation and evidence requirements.
Classify sources by authority, freshness, sensitivity and allowed use in decisions.
Keep representative domain cases and known failure cases for probabilistic behavior.
Show where foreign system or model semantics are translated before entering the local domain model.

core_rules: Context over service: draw semantic boundaries before deployment boundaries.
Decision over prompt: important business judgment must have an explicit domain owner and contract.
Agents never own business truth merely because they generated an answer.
Tools are domain contracts, not generic capabilities.
Events are useful as memory and evidence, not only as transport.
AI context is a first-class design artifact: its sources, freshness and authority must be known.
Autonomy is explicit, risk-tiered and preferably reversible.
Anti-corruption layers protect local semantics from external systems and from model-generated assumptions.
Deterministic invariants stay outside probabilistic judgment.
Increase autonomy only after observable evidence and evaluation show that the bounded action is reliable enough.

anti_patterns.problem: A general agent translates and coordinates every system without stable domain contracts.
anti_patterns.correction: Use explicit context contracts and let the agent operate through them.

anti_patterns.problem: Retrieved semantic memory is treated as current transactional truth.
anti_patterns.correction: Resolve authoritative state from the system of record before material decisions.

anti_patterns.problem: A probabilistic model is responsible for a rule that must always hold.
anti_patterns.correction: Encode the invariant deterministically and let AI work around it, not replace it.

anti_patterns.problem: One agent has broad access across contexts and can silently mix semantics and authority.
anti_patterns.correction: Scope agents by context, role, tool and autonomy level.

anti_patterns.problem: Critical business workflow exists only inside a long system prompt.
anti_patterns.correction: Model decisions, contracts, approvals and state transitions as durable domain artifacts.

anti_patterns.problem: Events are emitted as technical notifications without owner, stable meaning or schema evolution rule.
anti_patterns.correction: Publish domain facts with explicit ownership and contract.

anti_patterns.problem: Retrieval merges documents from several bounded contexts and makes conflicting terms look equivalent.
anti_patterns.correction: Preserve source context and translate semantics before using retrieved content in a decision.

sap_example.business_question: Can we keep the requested customer delivery promise, and what should we do if risk appears?

agent.name: Delivery Risk Advisor
may_do: recommend alternative plant or date when supported by valid domain services
prepare a proposed action for review
must_not_do: change a customer promise without the required authority
treat retrieved documentation as current order state

decision.deterministic_part: Availability, business invariants, authorization and executable transaction validation remain deterministic.
decision.ai_part: Explain trade-offs, connect evidence, rank permitted alternatives and prepare a recommendation.
decision.human_or_policy_part: Approve material promise changes unless a narrow A4 policy explicitly allows a reversible low-risk action.

agent_interface.instruction: Use this framework to analyze a business or software domain. Start from domain meaning and ownership, then classify decisions, evidence and allowed action. Do not start by assigning microservices, agents or databases.
analysis_order: classify deterministic invariants versus bounded judgment
place agents as actors inside contexts
safety_rules: Do not infer authority from data availability.
Do not classify model output as business truth.
Do not let semantic memory override a transactional source of record.
Do not delegate deterministic invariants to an LLM.
Do not cross bounded contexts without naming the contract and translation.
Do not recommend higher autonomy without a reversal path, evidence and evaluation cases.
